feature: The Brush sits right after Crop on a picture's tool bar
summary: On a picture the Brush is now the fourth tool, right after Crop, where the image mock draws it and where a Photoshop user looks first. It used to sit near the far end beside the paint bucket.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open any picture (a screenshot is fine) in a window about 1280 points wide. Walk: Scripts/playtest/brush-sits-after-crop-walk.json.

try.do: Open a screenshot and look at the tool bar under the picture.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Compare it with the image mock's tool bar: Brush is the fourth button in both.
Click the fourth button (the paintbrush) and paint a stroke on the picture.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press V, then B: the Brush lights again in the same slot.
Narrow the window until tools fold under More: the Brush stays on the bar longer than the drawing tools now.
Open a video: there is no Brush on its bar, and B is still the Blade.

evaluate: Is the Brush where your hand goes for it, right after Crop?
Does moving Measure and the drawing tools one slot to the right cost you anything you had learned?
Should the Brush and Crop sit in their own group with a hairline before them, the way the mock spaces them?
rough: The mock puts a gap between the wand and Crop and none after Brush; the shipped bar keeps its hairline after Measure, from the families the tool bar grouping task set (the-tool-bar-groups-tools-the-way-a-pro-editor-d).
The mock puts Measure near the end, after Shape; the shipped bar keeps it fifth, right after the Brush, as the tool bar grouping task placed it (the-tool-bar-groups-tools-the-way-a-pro-editor-d).

The mock draws Lasso, Eraser, Heal, Clone stamp, Patch and Dodge/Burn; none of them exist in the app yet. They belong to the selection and retouching epics, both staged later in the objectives (found-selection, image-retouch), and the Brush task a-brush-tool-paints-with-realistic-charcoal-chal kept E, J and S free for them, so no task is open for them now.
The mock's zoom slider and percentage are not on the bar: zoom is not a tool (your call on 2026-09-29).
Both shipped pictures show the window behind another app, so the lit Brush reads in its background look.
